about: Remarks at the start of an over: why the bowler's on, the new ball, the phase of the innings, and his plan.

any: SPIN ON -- THE PITCH IS OFFERING SOMETHING.
THE SPINNER ON NOW. THE SURFACE IS STARTING TO HELP.
{b} IS ON {r}. TIME FOR SOMETHING DIFFERENT.
BROUGHT ON FOR {b}, WHO'S ON {r}. A NEW PROBLEM FOR HIM.
THIS STAND IS WORTH {stand}. THEY NEED A BREAKTHROUGH.
TO BREAK A STAND OF {stand}.
THE NEW BALL IS DUE IN {n} OVERS.
{n} OVERS UNTIL THE NEW BALL.
THE NEW BALL IS AVAILABLE. WILL THEY TAKE IT?
NEW BALL AVAILABLE NOW.
THE NEW BALL IN HAND -- SHINY, HARD, DANGEROUS.
NEW BALL. IT'LL SWING AND BOUNCE.
NEW BALL, CLOSE CATCHERS. THE MOST DANGEROUS TIME TO BAT.
EARLY DAYS. THE BALL WILL DO A BIT NOW.
BOTH BATTERS LOOK SET. TIDY BOWLING, NOT THREATENING.
A PERIOD OF CONSOLIDATION. BOTH BATTERS IN.
{left} OVERS LEFT, {need} NEEDED. THIS IS WHERE IT GETS INTERESTING.
{need} FROM {left} OVERS. EVERY BALL MATTERS NOW.
{left} OVERS TO GO. TIME TO PUSH ON.
THE LAST {left} OVERS. EXPECT THE BIG SHOTS.
THE FIELD SAYS IT: EXPECT IT SHORT THIS OVER.
THEY'LL TEST HIM WITH THE SHORT BALL HERE, I THINK.
THIS WILL BE THE CORRIDOR: OUTSIDE OFF, AND WAIT.
HE'LL KEEP IT OUTSIDE OFF AND WAIT FOR THE MISTAKE.
A SQUEEZE ON: TIGHT LINES, NOTHING TO HIT.
THEY'RE GOING TO DRY UP THE RUNS THIS OVER.
WATCH FOR THE SET-UP: A FEW AWAY, THEN ONE BACK IN.
HE'LL SET HIM UP OUTSIDE OFF, THEN BRING ONE IN.
HE'LL GIVE IT AIR THIS OVER AND INVITE THE DRIVE.
TOSSING IT UP: HE WANTS HIM TO COME AT HIM.
HE'LL AIM FOR THE FOOTMARKS. A TOUGH OVER TO SURVIVE.
INTO THE ROUGH, I'D THINK. WATCH FOR THE BIG ONE.
